preconditions.description: The number of vertices in the graph is between 2 and 300,000.
The number of edges in the graph is between n - 1 and the maximum possible number of edges, which is either 300,000 or (n * (n - 1)) / 2, whichever is smaller.
The number of special vertices is between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= v_i <= n for v_i in special_vertices)
preconditions.description: The special vertices are numbered between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= c_i <= 10^9 for c_i in costs)
preconditions.description: The cost to make each vertex saturated is between 0 and 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= w_i <= 10^9 for w_i in weights)
preconditions.description: The weight of each edge if left undirected is between 0 and 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x_i, y_i <= n and x_i != y_i for (x_i, y_i) in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct vertices, each numbered between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: no edge is repeated in the input
preconditions.description: There are no duplicate edges in the input.
The graph is a single connected component.

postconditions.description: The output is a list of n integers, one for each vertex.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i] == max_profit_for_vertex(i) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: Each output integer is the maximum profit that can be achieved for the corresponding vertex by directing the edges appropriately.

invariants.expression: all(output[i] == max(profit_for_vertex(i, directed_edges, undirected_edges) for directed_edges in possible_directed_edges(i)) for i in range(n))
invariants.description: The maximum profit for each vertex is calculated by considering all possible ways to direct the edges such that the vertex is saturated.
